beats.text: Pong was not the first home video game.
beats.note: A defence engineer in New Hampshire built a multi-game TV console years before Atari.

beats.name: Ralph Baer
beats.role: Engineer at Sanders Associates in Nashua, New Hampshire. He began work on games that plug into a television.

beats.text: The Brown Box had a light gun and a golf putter.
beats.note: Its seventh version, TV Game Unit #7, was wrapped in brown wood-grain vinyl to look more appealing to investors.

beats.text: Nolan Bushnell saw the Odyssey demonstration.
beats.note: Atari's Pong followed. Magnavox and Sanders later sued Atari, and Atari settled and became a licensee.

beats.context: Baer's figure for Odyssey sales between 1972 and 1975, at $99.95 each.

beats.text: The patent fights around it paid out more than $100 million.

beats.line: Gaming history has an older chapter.
